newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Wednesday with investors covering short positions built on Tuesday when prices fell sharply, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 23,500 ($2,834) yuan per tonne, up 80 yuan. It opened lower at an intraday low of 23,400 yuan and hit a high of 23,540 yuan.
June fell 30 to 22,750, July rose 10 to 23,000, August rose 30 to 23,230, September gained 80 to 23,460 and November put on 100 to 23,520 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell sharply to 34,980 tonnes from 72,210 tonnes.
Traders said many investors built short positions on Tuesday when prices fell and covered them on Wednesday to avoid risk, pushing up prices.
Tuesday's prices took a tumble as rumours circulated on the market in that China's central reserve bureau was preparing to sell up to 50,000 tonnes of copper on the world market.

A bureau official said there were no such plans as no orders to do so had been received from the central government. The bureau acts only on directions from the State Council, or cabinet, the official said.
Despite Wednesday's rise, technical charts indicate a continued downward trend in the short term partly due to unpromising market fundamentals including weak physical prices, traders said.
Physical prices in the Shanghai area are hovering around 23,150 yuan per tonne.

The recent weak performance of the copper on the London Metal Exchange (LME) would also have a negative impact on the Shanghai market, traders said. LME copper faces resistance at $2,500 after a correction early this week. Analysts say it is vulnerable to the test of recent support around $2,470.
Three months copper closed at $2,490/94 on Tuesday.
One Shanghai trader said the key September contract on the local exchange could have difficulty recovering the 23,500-yuan level over the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. June lost 30 to 14,920, July 60 to 15,020, August 400 to 15,120, September 80 to 15,200 and October 100 to 15,200 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose slightly to 1,530 tonnes from 1,500 tonnes.
